notes: Six complete upright ink figures with large simple flint, hammer, hearth bowl, short spear, ochre handprint stone and berry basket. Two female-read figures at cells 2 and 4 (zero-based).

Acting includes focused wink, exuberant inventor, disapproving hearth keeper, frightened tracker, gleeful painter and suspicious collector. Inventor and artist have larger open grins than planned; individuality remains visible.
Cream tufted wraps, copper and indigo beads distinguish a coherent six-member family. Tablet, cylinder seal, grain, adze/ingot, reed bundle and jug/cup are visibly separate.
Cylinder seal is exaggerated and wide, tablet marks are decorative pseudo-writing, not a readable or verified inscription. Mouths and gaze differ across six faces; round goo anatomy is retained.

Six whole upright figures with compact wraps and readable brick/rod, balance, animal seal, bead strand/drill, scoop/pipe and cargo basket. Female-read cells 1 and 3 (zero-based), distinct from the other sheets' layout.
Some wrap motifs resemble Greek-key shapes; exact ancient dress is not asserted. Animal seal and scale remain stylized broad props. Filled wink eyelid and white-red-black eyes are visible.

Six distinct full ink silhouettes: many-handled jar keeper, frightened horn-grip athlete, flask painter, figure-eight-shield guard, ecstatic pigment painter and weary cargo carrier. Female-read cells 0 and 4 (zero-based).

The guard's helmet has a Greek/Roman-like crest, a period-mix deviation. Wraps and decorative motifs are fictional interpretations. Large uneven eyes and distinct closed, gritted, open and downturned mouths remain legible.
Six jade/red/cream workshop-court figures, including booklet, bead drill, cacao vessel, stone basket, ball and weaving shuttle. Female-read cells 2 and 5 (zero-based).

The mason's planned square is absent; the basket and held stone carry the role. Decorative booklet dots and jade motifs are not asserted as readable ancient writing. Expressions are varied and all dark eyelids filled.
Six travel/workshop figures with individual route sheet, textile bolt, spice vessels, tabbed book, tea kettle and large-clasp chest. Female-read cells 1 and 4 (zero-based).

Clothing is a deliberately mixed caravan-route vocabulary rather than one reconstructed historical uniform. A similar surprised mouth occupies top-right here and in Sumer, but face/eyelid silhouettes and prop situations remain distinct.
